Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires make their way back out to the middle, and the Bangladesh players can be seen waiting patiently near the boundary ropes. It will be the inexperienced duo of Azan Awais and Abdullah Fazal to open the innings for Pakistan. Taskin Ahmed will take the new ball for the hosts. Let's go...
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

A mountain too high? Pakistan won't be all too pleased that they have to come back out and bat in the final half an hour or so of Day 3. This could be a tricky period, but on the other hand, they will be pleased that they haven't conceded even more runs. With the ball, Khurram Shahzad picked up another four-fer, matching his effort in the first innings and after toiling long and hard, Sajid Khan got three wickets towards the end of the innings to close things off. Hasan Ali and Mohammad Abbas bowled well in patches, but overall, it was an underwhelming display of bowling. Right then, about 8-10 overs left in the day, time and light permitting and Bangladesh will be eager to pick up early wickets. Can Pakistan's openers weather the storm and remain unscathed heading into Day 4? Let's find out as the chase is up next.

Rahim leads the charge for Bangladesh - Finally, after a bit over 102 overs, Pakistan have managed to bowl out the hosts in their second innings, but not before Bangladesh have managed to pile on a big lead. The target for Pakistan will be 437 big runs, and with over 2 days still remaining in the game, it is fair to say that we will get a result. Coming back to Bangladesh's batting, their top order didn't fire as expected again, and once again, it was Litton Das who provided a lot of impetus to the innings. Mushfiqur Rahim played second fiddle but once Das got out, Rahim took charge and built a few crucial stands with the lower order to score a fine hundred.

OUT! CAUGHT! Finally, the marathon knock of Mushfiqur Rahim comes to an end and with that, Bangladesh are bowled out for 390. Pakistan will need 437 to win this Test and level the series. Tossed up, around middle and off, Mushfiqur Rahim goes down on a knee and looks for a slog sweep at it. Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back folks, for the last session of Day 3! The players have already entered the field and are taking their respective positions. Pakistan can opt for their second new ball in just two overs. Sajid Khan will start after the Tea break with a slip and a short leg in place. Away we go...
... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ...

The visitors continue to toil in the field - Another long session for Pakistan, especially the pacers, and they are just going more and more behind in this game with every passing session. Khurram Shahzad has been the lone bright spot in both innings so far, and he's taken 4 out of the 6 wickets so far. Hasan Ali too bowled well in patches, making good use of the short ball, but he's been inconsistent as well, like the rest of the bowlers. Pakistan need something to give here, as even with inclement weather on the cards, there's still a long way to go in this Test match and they wouldn't want to concede a huge target. Stick around as the final session on Day 3 will begin at 9.02 am GMT.

The veteran stands tall - Mushfiqur Rahim is still out there, batting on 90, and he's taking the hosts to a commanding position in this game. The session began with Rahim and Litton Das stitching together a 123-run stand, but Bangladesh then lost a couple of wickets and it felt like Pakistan would be able to get back in the game. However, Rahim took matters into his own hands and started playing a few more shots, racking up some boundaries as well. Taijul Islam did well to fend off a barrage of short balls and is still out there batting on 8. Bangladesh will now look to take the lead beyond the 400-run mark.

SESSION SUMMARY - 26 overs, 104 runs, and 2 wickets. End of another productive session for Bangladesh, and they stretched their lead to 353 runs, with still 4 wickets in hand. As for Pakistan, they made a couple of inroads in this session, but there were too many No Balls towards the end of the session, and the runs flowed thick and fast.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back to resume the action post Lunch break! The players of Pakistan are striding toward their respective fielding positions. Litton Das and Mushfiqur Rahim will be continuing their inning. Das will take the strike and he is just two runs away from his 20th Test half-century. Khurram Shahzad will start the proceedings after the break with a slip and a gully in place. Let's play...
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

Tigers chasing history - The figure of 300 runs as a lead looms large as the realistic target Bangladesh will be aiming for. If the partnership continues to flourish in the afternoon session, Bangladesh could set Pakistan a chase in excess of 300 on a deteriorating Sylhet surface. With rain still lurking in the forecast and the pitch offering something to the bowlers, the hosts will want to bat deep into the day and effectively seal this Test, and with it, a historic series sweep that would rank among Bangladesh's finest achievements in Test cricket. We will be back with the post-Lunch session at 6.40 am GMT.

Pakistan need to uplift their game - For Pakistan, Khurram Shahzad was the standout bowler, who got the wicket of the opposition skipper, but after that, the bowlers failed to capitalize. The changes haven't had any impact for them as well. Yes, there were few instances where they were really close to finding their dismissal, where it's the run-out chance or the caught behind, but failed to get the final result right.

The veteran pair anchors the inning - After the fall of the fourth wicket, the session saw a familiar face step up once again for the hosts. Bangladesh lead by 249 runs heading into the Lunch break, and with Litton Das at the crease on 48 and Mushfiqur Rahim alongside him on 39, Bangladesh are 203 for 4 after 53 overs. The experienced duo of Litton and Mushfiqur, two of Bangladesh's most battle-hardened performers, have combined to steady the innings after the loss of wickets in the top order, and their partnership through the final stages of the session has given the hosts real momentum heading into the afternoon.

LUNCH ON DAY 3 - In this session, a total of 26.2 overs were bowled, where Bangladesh scored 93 and lost just a wicket. What a session it was for the host and it's once again Litton Das, the centurion from the previous inning, who stepped up to take matters in hand. Bangladesh resumed Day 3 on 110 for 3 in their second innings, already holding a lead of 156 runs and with the intent to bat Pakistan out of the Day entirely. Mahmudul Hasan Joy set the tone the previous evening by playing his natural, aggressive game, but by the end of Day 2, Bangladesh had lost three wickets already. However, Pakistan's bowlers came out with discipline and purpose, and the morning session saw the wicket of Bangladesh's skipper Shanto dismissed by Khurram Shahzad, and the tourists managed to apply consistent pressure in the first hour of the day.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set! The two umpires are striding toward the center of the park. The players of Pakistan have taken their respective fielding positions. Now, if you don't remember, just before the Stumps on Day 2, Khurram Shahzad found a dismissal of Mominul Haque. Mushfiqur Rahim is the new batter on the crease. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT ON DAY 3 - Athar Ali Khan is pitchside. He starts off saying that Bangladesh are in the driving seat with a 157-run lead and 7 wickets left. The pitch's tricky, Litton Das's century was sublime, but it's no easy ride for batters. He thinks Pakistan's under pressure, their bowlers need to wrap up Bangladesh's innings cheaply or it'll be a tough total to chase in the fourth innings. The pitch's similar to before, with patches helping bowlers. Both teams' bowlers exploited it well, picking up wickets.

A word from the Bangladesh camp, Mohammad Abbas -He was straight up being asked about the momentum change on Day 2, on that he replied that he was not at his best initially, but later on he got his rhythm. He also adds that it does happen in test cricket, sometimes the opposition dominates as well. Ends up saying that it is very important to draw the test series and they will be doing it at any cost.

Mahmudul Hasan Joy is up for a chat - Hasan Joy says that he was very happy that he performed better than in the previous inning. However, he was a bit shaky as he batted well in the previous test match. On batting on Day 2, he says that he was very happy as the sun came out late. On playing his attacking shots, he says that he felt the surface was good to bat as the deliveries were coming nicely to the bat, which gave him more confidence to play his shots. On being asked about Bangladesh's plan on Day 3, he says that they don't have a certain plan in their mind, but they would like to take time and continue building their innings.

The tactical showdown - For Bangladesh, the strategy today is simple, maintain relentless pressure by playing long into the day's play. Their batters need to stick together and let the bat do the talking to post a massive total. Conversely, Pakistan needs their bowlers to make early inroads and wrap this Bangladesh innings to a manageable total. The outcome of these next three sessions could ultimately dictate who walks away with a victory.

Pakistan's battle for survival - Pakistan faces a monumental task and must show immense resilience to claw their way back into contention. The immediate priority for their bowlers to bowl Bangladesh out for as less score as they can from here on. It will then be on the batters to put patient partnerships and occupy the crease for multiple sessions. Taking wickets is a must for the visitors before the game drifts out of their hands.

Bangladesh in the driver’s seat - Bangladesh enters day three in a commanding position after dominating the opening phases of this match. Their top-order batters applied immense discipline, wearing down the opposition bowlers to post a massive total on the scoreboard. Furthermore, their spin attack has already found purchase on a rapidly deteriorating surface, putting immediate pressure on the visitors. This clinical execution across both departments has given the hosts a distinct advantage.

Welcome to Day 3 - Welcome, cricket fans, to day three of this gripping Test match between Bangladesh and Pakistan. Traditionally known as moving day, this middle phase of the match is where the game truly shifts shape, setting up the final result. The morning session today promises high tension and crucial tactical battles as both teams fight to seize control of the sessions ahead.

That's a wrap from Day 2 - Right then, that is it from Day 2 of this 2nd Test between Bangladesh and Pakistan, where the hosts have firmly seized control of the contest, while the visitors will be hoping for a strong comeback on the moving day. The action will resume for Day 3 on 18th May, Sunday at 4 am GMT, but do join us early for all the build-up. Until then, cheers!

Joy's fifty keeps Bangladesh on top - Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Mominul Haque looked solid in the final session, scoring at a brisk rate while keeping the Pakistan bowlers at bay. Joy brought up a fine half-century and the pair added 76 runs together before Mohammad Abbas finally broke the stand. Sajid Khan found some turn in the latter stages of the day and did trouble the batters, but it was Khurram Shahzad who delivered the breakthrough in the final over, dismissing Mominul and giving Pakistan a slight glimmer of hope.

Bangladesh continue to call shots - The afternoon session belonged largely to Bangladesh as they struck regularly once the Babar-Salman partnership was broken. Babar brought up a gritty fifty before departing for 68, while Nahid Rana and Taijul Islam kept Pakistan under pressure with timely breakthroughs. Just when Bangladesh looked set for a huge lead, Sajid Khan counterattacked with a rapid cameo to drag Pakistan to 232 and keep the deficit down to 46. Bangladesh then batted positively before Tea, extending their lead past 100 with only one wicket lost.

Babar holds firm after early collapse - Pakistan began the morning session steadily but Bangladesh quickly seized control through Taskin Ahmed and Mehidy Hasan Miraz, reducing the visitors to 79/4 before Lunch. Babar Azam held firm under pressure and stitched together a valuable stand with Salman Agha to steady the innings, ensuring Pakistan went into the break still fighting despite trailing by over 180 runs.

Pakistan strike late after tough day - SESSION SUMMARY - 136 runs and 5 wickets in 29.2 overs! Well, a wicket in the final over has slightly dented what was otherwise a dominant day for Bangladesh. They not only ensured Pakistan stayed well short of their first-innings total, but also stretched their lead to 156 and are now firmly on course to set a daunting target for the visitors. Pakistan did not have much to celebrate throughout the day, but that late breakthrough has at least given them a small moment of encouragement heading into Day 3.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! The two batters were playing it safe so that they could survive the day, but well, Khurram Shahzad gets the better and bags his second. He bangs hard on the good length to offer a bouncer, into the corridor of uncertainty. Haque looks to guide it to deep third, but induces an outside edge. The ball flies to the left of the keeper and Mohammad Rizwan shuffles to take the catch. Bangladesh lose their third wicket and it will be STUMPS ON DAY 2.
